Service.Name: WMS
Service.Title: GWIS
Service.Abstract: The Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS) supports the services in charge of the protection of forests against fires and provides the European Commission services and the European Parliament with updated and reliable information on wildland fires at the global level.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.fwi
Layer.Title: ecmwf.fwi
Layer.Abstract: Fire Weather Index (FWI) from ECMWF reanalysis data. The FWI is a numerical rating of fire intensity and potential fire behavior, based on weather conditions such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and precipitation. It is commonly used in wildfire management and forecasting to assess fire risk and guide firefighting efforts.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.ffmc
Layer.Title: ecmwf.ffmc
Layer.Abstract: Fine Fuel Moisture Code (FFMC) from ECMWF reanalysis data. The FFMC is a numerical rating of the moisture content of fine fuels, such as grass and leaves, which can influence the ignition and spread of wildfires. It is commonly used in wildfire management and forecasting to assess fire risk and guide firefighting efforts.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.dmc
Layer.Title: ecmwf.dmc
Layer.Abstract: Duff Moisture Code (DMC) from ECMWF reanalysis data. The DMC is a numerical rating of the moisture content of medium-sized fuels, such as shrubs and small branches, which can influence the ignition and spread of wildfires. It is commonly used in wildfire management and forecasting to assess fire risk and guide firefighting efforts.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.dc
Layer.Title: ecmwf.dc
Layer.Abstract: Drought Code (DC) from ECMWF reanalysis data. The DC is a numerical rating of the moisture content of deep, compacted organic layers, which can influence the ignition and spread of wildfires. It is commonly used in wildfire management and forecasting to assess fire risk and guide firefighting efforts.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.isi
Layer.Title: ecmwf.isi
Layer.Abstract: Initial Spread Index (ISI) from ECMWF reanalysis data. The ISI is a numerical rating of the expected rate of fire spread immediately after ignition, based on weather conditions such as wind speed and fine fuel moisture content. It is commonly used in wildfire management and forecasting to assess fire risk and guide firefighting efforts.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.bui
Layer.Title: ecmwf.bui
Layer.Abstract: Buildup Index (BUI) from ECMWF reanalysis data. The BUI is a numerical rating of the total amount of fuel available for combustion, based on weather conditions such as precipitation and temperature. It is commonly used in wildfire management and forecasting to assess fire risk and guide firefighting efforts.

Layer.Name: mf025.fwi
Layer.Title: mf025.fwi
Layer.Abstract: The GWIS Meteo‑France‑based Fire‑Weather Index (FWI) layer provides a daily raster of fire‑weather conditions across the European Union. It is derived each day from Meteo‑France surface observations and short‑range forecasts (temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and precipitation) using the Canadian FWI system. The product is updated in near‑real‑time and supplies a quantitative measure of fire‑danger potential to support the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) in risk assessment, early‑warning mapping and operational decision‑making.

Layer.Name: nasa_geos5.fwi
Layer.Title: nasa_geos5.fwi
Layer.Abstract: The GWIS NASA GEOS‑5 based Fire‑Weather Index (FWI) layer provides a daily raster of fire‑weather conditions for the European Union. The index is computed each day from atmospheric variables (temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and precipitation) derived from the GEOS‑5 global reanalysis and forecast system. Using the Canadian FWI methodology, the product delivers a quantitative measure of fire‑danger potential that is integrated into the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) to support fire‑risk assessment, early‑warning mapping and operational decision‑making.

Layer.Name: nasa_geos5.ffmc
Layer.Title: nasa_geos5.ffmc
Layer.Abstract: Fine Fuel Moisture Code (FFMC) - a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) system that represents the moisture content of fine fuels, such as grass and leaves. The FFMC is calculated based on temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation data. It provides an indication of the ease of ignition and the potential for fire spread in fine fuels. Higher FFMC values indicate drier conditions and a greater likelihood of fire ignition and spread.

Layer.Name: nasa_geos5.dmc
Layer.Title: nasa_geos5.dmc
Layer.Abstract: Duff Moisture Code (DMC) - a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) system that represents the moisture content of medium-sized fuels, such as small branches and twigs. The DMC is calculated based on temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation data. It provides an indication of the potential for fire spread in medium-sized fuels. Higher DMC values indicate drier conditions and a greater likelihood of fire spread in medium-sized fuels.

Layer.Name: nasa_geos5.dc
Layer.Title: nasa_geos5.dc
Layer.Abstract: Drought Code (DC) - a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) system that represents the moisture content of deep, compact organic layers, such as peat and humus. The DC is calculated based on temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation data. It provides an indication of the potential for fire spread in deep organic layers. Higher DC values indicate drier conditions and a greater likelihood of fire spread in deep organic layers.

Layer.Name: nasa_geos5.isi
Layer.Title: nasa_geos5.isi
Layer.Abstract: Initial Spread Index (ISI) - a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) system that represents the potential for fire spread in the early stages of a fire. The ISI is calculated based on temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation data. It provides an indication of the rate of fire spread in the initial stages of a fire. Higher ISI values indicate drier conditions and a greater likelihood of rapid fire spread in the early stages.

Layer.Name: nasa_geos5.bui
Layer.Title: nasa_geos5.bui
Layer.Abstract: Buildup Index (BUI) - a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) system that represents the potential for fire spread in larger fuels, such as logs and large branches. The BUI is calculated based on temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation data. It provides an indication of the potential for fire spread in larger fuels. Higher BUI values indicate drier conditions and a greater likelihood of fire spread in larger fuels.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.extra.lightning
Layer.Title: ecmwf.extra.lightning
Layer.Abstract: The GWIS ECMWF Lightning layer provides a near-real-time raster of lightning flash density derived from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Integrated Forecast System. Updated hourly, the product shows the estimated number of cloud-to-ground flashes per km² for the preceding 24 hours at a spatial resolution of approximately 0.1° (≈10 km). It covers the whole European Union and is intended to support the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) by enhancing fire-danger mapping, early-warning alerts and operational decision-making where lightning-ignited fires are a significant risk.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.extra.totalprecipitation
Layer.Title: ecmwf.extra.totalprecipitation
Layer.Abstract: The GWIS ECMWF Total Precipitation layer provides a near-real-time forecast raster of accumulated precipitation derived from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Integrated Forecast System. Updated sub-daily, the product displays accumulated total precipitation in millimeters (mm) at a spatial resolution of approximately 0.07° (~7 km). It supports the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) and Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS) for fire danger assessment and weather monitoring.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.extra.windspeed
Layer.Title: ecmwf.extra.windspeed
Layer.Abstract: The GWIS ECMWF 10m Wind Speed layer provides a near-real-time forecast raster of 10-meter wind speed derived from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Integrated Forecast System. Updated sub-daily, the product displays 10m wind speed in meters per second (m/s) at a spatial resolution of approximately 0.07° (~7 km). It supports the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) and Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS) for fire danger assessment and weather monitoring.

Layer.Name: ecmwf.extra.wind.uv
Layer.Title: ecmwf.extra.wind.uv
Layer.Abstract: The GWIS ECMWF 10m Wind Vector layer provides a near-real-time forecast of 10-meter wind speed and direction derived from U and V components of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Integrated Forecast System.

Layer.Name: all.hs.grid
Layer.Title: all.hs.grid
Layer.Abstract: Active fires (MODIS + VIIRS), the period given by TIME, by default the same as the point layers, aggregated per 0.1 degree cell: shown instead of the individual detections when zoomed out past 1:10000000. Each cell is coloured by the age of its most recent detection, in the same classes as the detections themselves.
